newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam president says health recovering.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam president says health recovering.

text.p: Vietnam's President, General Le Duc Anh, issued his first public statement on Friday since suffering a stroke in mid-November, saying he was recovering.
The brief statement, carried by the official Vietnam News Agency, quoted Anh, 76, as saying he wished to thank people who had sent messages of concern during his illness.

"The illness is now over. My health is in the process of recovery. On behalf of my family and myself I would like to sincerely thank everyone, and would like to send my best wishes to all the people, cadres and friends," he was quoted as saying.
The VNA statement was the first to quote Anh in person since he fell ill.
VNA added that senior members of the elite politburo had visited Anh on Friday and expressed the hope that he would be well enough to return to work soon.
Le Duc Anh, the most powerful military figure in Vietnam, is a member of the country's leadership triumvirate alongside Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet.
He was admitted to a Hanoi hospital last November suffering problems related to high blood pressure. It later became apparent he had suffered a stroke.
But within hours of his hospital admission a veil of secrecy was drawn over details of his health.

Aside from a passing reference to Anh's absence from a state function in November, Friday's statement marked the first significant mention of his illness in domestic media. The announcement comes just days ahead of Vietnam's Tet lunar new year festival. The holiday, which runs from February 6 to 10, is the most important festival of the year.
Traditionally the president, as head of state, issues a nationwide message on television, radio and in newspapers to mark the occasion.
